fullPassage:
[1번] One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.

[2번] Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our identity. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!

[3번] Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.

[4번] Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.

[5번] Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."

[6번] The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should assume that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.

[7번] Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.

[8번] In the Parana Delta near Buenos Aires, Argentina, is a small island called "The Eye," which floats in the middle of a small lake that is about 120 meters in diameter. It was accidentally discovered by Argentinian film director Sergio Neuspiller during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials. Interestingly, both the island and the lake are perfectly circular. What's more, the lake that surrounds the island is extremely cold and clear — an unusual phenomenon for the area. So mysterious is the island that people have wondered if it was created naturally or by aliens. Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: what → that (앞에 선행사 conditions가 있으므로 관계대명사 that/which)
det.analysis:
① what: 'One of the most difficult conditions ___ patients deal with'을 보세요. 밑줄 앞에 꾸며 줄 명사(선행사) conditions가 있어요. 선행사가 있을 때는 관계대명사 that(또는 which)을 써야 해요. what은 선행사가 없을 때 '~하는 것'이라는 뜻으로 쓰므로 여기서는 틀려요. ←정답

③ sense: 'patients cannot ___'는 조동사 cannot 뒤라 동사원형 sense가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

④ suffering: 'a woman ___ from damage'는 명사 woman을 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사라 suffering이 맞아요. 적절합니다.
det.tip: 선행사(conditions)가 있으면 관계대명사 that/which. what(X, 선행사 없을 때만)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: deeper → higher (녹음은 뼈 전달이 빠져 예상보다 더 높게 들림)
det.analysis:
① bother(신경 쓰이게 하다): '대화 땐 신경 쓰이지 않는다' — 적절

④ identity(정체성): '목소리는 정체성의 일부' — 적절
det.tip: 녹음 = 뼈 전달(깊은 소리) 없음 → 예상보다 higher(더 높게). deeper는 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 draw the purest essence out of something이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: draw the purest essence out of something = 어떤 것에서 가장 순수하고 핵심적인 부분을 뽑아내다
det.analysis:
밑줄 부분에서 'draw ... out of(~에서 이끌어 내다/뽑아내다)'와 'the purest essence(가장 순수한 정수)'가 핵심이에요. 즉 어떤 물질에서 가장 순수하고 값진 핵심 성분을 뽑아낸다는 뜻이에요. 화학자들이 이를 액체(증류)에 적용해 순수한 술을 얻은 흐름도 이를 뒷받침해요.

❌ ① completely destroy the original shape of a solid(고체의 원래 모양을 완전히 파괴한다) — 파괴가 아니라 핵심을 뽑아내는 것이에요.

❌ ② hide a substance's true color from other people(물질의 진짜 색을 감춘다) — 감추는 게 아니에요.

❌ ③ mix several different liquids into one solution(여러 액체를 하나로 섞는다) — 섞는 게 아니라 순수한 정수를 뽑아내는 것이에요.

✅ ④ extract the most refined and valuable part of a material(물질에서 가장 정제되고 값진 부분을 추출한다) — '가장 순수한 정수를 뽑아낸다'는 밑줄의 뜻과 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: draw ... out of = 뽑아내다, the purest essence = 가장 순수한 정수 → 핵심 성분을 추출한다

Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: being biased=편향되는 것 / losing money=돈을 잃는 것 / making friends=친구를 사귀는 것 / feeling proud=자랑스러워하는 것
det.analysis:
① being biased: 어떤 지위든 될 수 있다고 가정함으로써, 현재 자신의 처지에 의해 '편향되는 것'을 피할 수 있다는 흐름과 맞아요. ←정답

② losing money: 돈을 잃는 것 — 문맥과 무관해요.

③ making friends: 친구를 사귀는 것 — 문맥과 무관해요.

④ feeling proud: 자랑스러워하는 것 — 문맥과 무관해요.
det.tip: you can avoid __________ by your current situation → 편향되는 것(being biased)

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문 S4·S6 'so does its quickness' + 'along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes'를 바꿔 말함 → 일치

몽구스는 이빨이 없어 오직 두꺼운 털로만 몸을 지킨다.

② damaged: 'When it is ___'는 수동태(be + 과거분사)라 damaged가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

③ shave: 'he might only ___'는 조동사 might 뒤라 동사원형 shave가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

④ applies: 'She would only ___ it'에서 앞에 조동사 would가 있어요. 조동사 뒤에는 항상 동사원형이 오므로 applies(-s가 붙은 형태)가 아니라 apply가 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: 조동사(would) 뒤에는 동사원형. would apply(O) / would applies(X)

questions.passage: Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is __________. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목소리가 낯설면 속상한 이유 → 목소리가 '우리 정체성의 중요한 일부'이기 때문
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'Our voice is ___. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought(우리 목소리는 ___. 그래서 생각과 다르면 속상하다)'예요. 낯설 때 속상한 이유는 목소리가 '나'와 깊이 연결되기 때문이죠.

① an important part of our identity(우리 정체성의 중요한 일부): 낯설면 속상한 이유와 자연스럽게 연결 ←정답

② a minor cause of confusion(사소한 혼란의 원인): 속상함의 근거로 약함

③ a useless piece of data(쓸모없는 정보 조각): 문맥과 무관

④ a common source of stress(흔한 스트레스 원인): 정체성 이야기와 어긋남
det.tip: 낯선 목소리에 속상한 이유 → 목소리 = 정체성(identity)의 일부

ch: an important part of our identity

questions.passage: Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as <u>those</u> of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 those가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: those = 앞에 나온 복수 명사 the melatonin levels(멜라토닌 수치)를 대신함
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 those는 같은 명사의 반복을 피하려고 쓰는 대명사예요. 두 문장 앞의 'compared the melatonin levels of two groups'에서 나온 '멜라토닌 수치(the melatonin levels)'를 가리켜요.

① 고글을 쓰지 않은 집단의 사람들: those는 '사람들'이 아니라 '수치'를 받음
② 실험에 사용된 특수 고글: 고글이 아니라 수치
③ 여러 집단의 멜라토닌 수치: those가 대신하는 것은 the melatonin levels(멜라토닌 수치) ←정답
④ 무지개를 이루는 여러 색: 문맥과 무관
det.tip: the same as those of the first group → those = the melatonin levels(멜라토닌 수치)

questions.passage: Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry <u>their</u> own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 their가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: their own food = 달리기 선수들(the runners) 자신의 음식
det.analysis:
밑줄 their는 바로 앞의 'the runners(달리기 선수들)'를 가리켜요. 'the runners have to carry their own food'는 '선수들이 자신의 음식을 지니고 가야 한다'는 뜻이에요.

① 대회 주최 측: 필수품을 제공하는 쪽이지 음식을 챙기는 주체가 아님 — 오답

② 대회에 참가한 달리기 선수들: 음식을 직접 챙기는 주체가 선수들이므로 their = 선수들 ←정답

③ 관중들: 본문에 등장하지 않음 — 오답

④ 아마존의 동물들: 본문에 등장하지 않음 — 오답
det.tip: the runners have to carry their own food → their = 선수들

questions.passage: Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③이 본문(alcohol의 어원이 눈화장 재료에 있음)과 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치 — 이집트인들은 광물을 '가열해(heated)' 승화시켰지 액체를 얼린 게 아니에요.

❌ ② 불일치 — kohl은 라틴어가 아니라 '얼룩/칠'을 뜻하는 아랍어예요.

✅ ③ 일치 — alcohol은 눈화장(kohl/al-kohl)이라는 고대의 화장 재료에서 유래했어요. 어원의 뿌리가 화장 재료에 있다는 진술과 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ④ 불일치 — 화학자들은 용어를 새로 만든 게 아니라 옛 교재에서 '발견했어요(discovered)'.
det.tip: alcohol의 뿌리 = 눈화장(kohl) → ③ 일치

ch: 고대 이집트인들은 액체를 얼려 검은 가루를 만들었다.
kohl은 술을 뜻하는 라틴어에서 나온 말이다.
alcohol이라는 단어의 뿌리는 고대의 화장 재료에 있다.
화학자들은 자신들이 새로 만든 용어를 옛 책에 기록해 두었다.

questions.passage: The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first ①<u>proposed</u> by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should ②<u>assumes</u> that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely ③<u>reject</u> slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally ④<u>adopt</u> fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: assumes → assume (조동사 should 뒤에는 동사원형)
det.analysis:
① proposed: 'a concept that was first proposed by'는 'be동사 + 과거분사'의 수동태예요. 적절합니다.

② assumes: 'you should ___ that ~'에서 조동사 should 뒤에는 항상 동사원형이 와야 해요. 그래서 assumes가 아니라 assume이 맞아요. ←정답

③ reject: 'people would likely reject slavery' 조동사 would + 동사원형 — 적절합니다.

④ adopt: 'society would naturally adopt' 조동사 would + 동사원형 — 적절합니다.
det.tip: 조동사(should, will, would...) 바로 뒤 동사는 항상 동사원형. should assume

questions.passage: Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문 S8 'Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose'를 바꿔 말함 → 일치
det.analysis:
① 성체 몽구스를 죽일 만큼 강한 독이 흔치 않다 = 'Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose'를 바꿔 말함 ←정답(일치)
② 물리면 대부분 즉사? 본문은 오히려 물려도 대개 '살아남는다(survive)'고 함 — 불일치
③ 땅속으로 숨음? 본문은 숨는 게 아니라 뱀을 사냥·격퇴한다고 함 — 불일치
④ 이빨이 무뎌 뼈를 못 부숨? 본문은 '28개의 날카로운(sharp) 이빨'로 뼈를 '부술(crack)' 수 있다고 함 — 불일치
det.tip: Rare ... venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose = 성체를 죽일 독은 드묾(일치)

ch: 성체 몽구스를 죽일 만큼 강력한 뱀의 독은 흔하지 않다.
몽구스는 뱀에게 물리면 그 독 때문에 대부분 즉사한다.
몽구스는 뱀을 피해 주로 땅속으로 숨는 습성이 있다.
몽구스는 이빨이 무뎌 단단한 뼈는 부수지 못한다.

questions.passage: Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's __________ (unusual) cold, clear water.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: unusual(흔치 않은, 형용사) → unusually(유난히, 부사). 형용사 cold를 꾸미는 부사 자리
det.analysis:
빈칸이 든 부분은 'the lake's __________ (unusual) cold, clear water'예요.

① 괄호 안 unusual은 '흔치 않은'이라는 형용사예요. 그런데 빈칸 바로 뒤에는 cold(차가운)라는 또 다른 형용사가 있어요.

② 형용사(cold)를 꾸며 주는 말은 부사라야 해요. 그래서 형용사 unusual을 부사 unusually(유난히, 이례적으로)로 바꿔 'unusually cold(유난히 차가운)'로 써야 해요.
det.tip: 형용사(cold)를 꾸미는 자리 → 부사 unusually (unusual은 형용사)

questions.passage: One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, __________ of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (8단어) (영어로)
'뇌의 왼쪽에 손상을 입은 한 남성'
[조건] (1) a, damage, left, man, side, the, to, with을 모두 사용
(2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: a man with damage to the left side = 뇌의 왼쪽에 손상을 입은 한 남성
det.analysis:
핵심 명사 'a man(한 남성)'을 먼저 놓고, 그 남성을 꾸미는 말을 전치사 with(~을 가진)로 이어요. 'with damage'는 '손상을 가진', 즉 '손상을 입은'이라는 뜻이에요.

'왼쪽에'라는 위치는 to the left side로 나타내요.

순서: a + man + with + damage + to + the + left + side = a man with damage to the left side.
det.tip: 명사(a man) + with(~을 가진) + damage + to the left side(왼쪽에) = 왼쪽에 손상을 입은 남성

questions.wa: a man with damage to the left side
accept: a man with damage to the left side

it(3인칭 단수) + moves(동사에 -s)

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (7단어) (영어로)
'파란빛은 우리의 멜라토닌 분비에 영향을 준다'

questions.passage: Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging __________ (competition). The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: competition(대회) → competitions(복수형). 'one of the + 최상급 + 복수명사' 구조
det.analysis: competition을 복수형 competitions로 바꿔요. 'one of the + 최상급 + 복수명사(~ 중 하나)' 구조라서 뒤에는 반드시 복수명사가 와요. 'one of the world's most challenging competitions' = 세계에서 가장 힘든 대회들 중 하나.
det.tip: one of the most + 복수명사 → competitions
